issues.description: The attend(course:) method signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template require a single-parameter method attend(course: Course?), and the solution's Client calls myself.attend(course: swiftCourse). However, the Solution's Developer implementation declares attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool), introducing an extra parameter. This mismatch both deviates from the specification and creates an internal inconsistency in the solution (Client calls the single-argument form while Developer defines a two-argument form), which will confuse students and can lead to compilation or usage errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Developer.attend method signature consistent with the problem statement and template: declare func attend(course: Course?) { ... } in the solution. Alternatively, if the extra parameter is intentional, update the problem statement, template, and all call sites (e.g., Client) to include the new parameter or provide a default value (e.g., forCredit: Bool = true) so signatures and usages match.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template both specify an instance method attend(course:) on Developer that takes a single optional Course argument. The solution implementation changes the API to attend(course:forCredit:), adding an extra parameter (forCredit: Bool). This mismatch means students following the problem/template cannot directly compare their attend(course:) implementation with the solution and may be confused about the intended method signature and usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's Developer.attend method use the same signature as the problem and template (attend(course: Course?)) or, if the extra parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and template to describe and include the forCredit parameter so all artifacts share the same API.
